title: Randomized execution as deterministic execution on paired inputs
statement: Let $p$ be a public-coin protocol with shared randomness in $\Omega$, Alice's private input in $X$, and Bob's in $Y$, producing an output in $\alpha$. Then for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, and $\omega \in \Omega$, the randomized execution of $p$ on $x$, $y$ with random string $\omega$ equals the execution of the underlying deterministic protocol on the paired inputs $(\omega, x)$ and $(\omega, y)$.
hypotheses_covered: public-coin protocol p over randomness Omega, inputs X, Y, output alpha
shared random string omega in Omega
replaced:
For any public-coin protocol $p$, inputs $x$, $y$, and randomness $\omega$,
$p.\texttt{rrun}\,x\,y\,\omega = p.\texttt{run}\,(\omega, x)\,(\omega, y)$.
This is a definitional unfolding used as a \texttt{simp} lemma.
